title: Adaptive batch hysteresis and KV-Cache Coordinator refactor
creator: Lina Park
description: Summary: This ticket refactors the continuous batching path and the KV cache eviction/coordination logic into two collaborating components: an Adaptive Batch Controller (ABC) with hysteresis and token-adaptive lane sizing, and a lightweight KV-Cache Coordinator (KCC) that centralizes eviction policy, lease-based ownership, and cross-shard reclamation. Goals: reduce tail latency spikes during rapid traffic oscillations, eliminate a global batcher mutex that causes latency amplification at high concurrency, improve steady-state token throughput by ~5-12% on p99-sensitive workloads, and make cache eviction behavior predictable for multi-tenant Dedicated pools. Scope: code refactor of the hot-path batching loop in serving/runtime/batcher, introduce a small coordinator service in serving/runtime/cache, upgrade the internal kvc library to v2.3 for lockless lease APIs, and add telemetry and feature flags for staged rollout. This is strictly a refactor and API-compatible from the HTTP surface; low-risk behavior changes are guarded behind flags and can be disabled at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: No change in REST contract or SDK behaviors for existing clients (backwards compatible),
P99 tail latency for standard text-gen synthetic workload improves or is within 3% of baseline across canary runs,
End-to-end cache hit ratio is steady and per-tenant cache ownership metrics are emitted to the console with new KCC gauges,
Canary rollback must restore old batcher path via a runtime feature flag within 2 minutes,
Automated unit and integration tests added for lease handoff and lane-resizing logic.
notes: Design debt: previous continuous-batcher merged queueing and eviction callbacks which led to cross-cutting locks under bursty loads. This refactor attempts to move lock contention out of the hot path by (1) introducing per-lane MPMC queues with atomic occupancy counters, (2) hysteresis thresholds to avoid oscillation when request rates hover near size boundaries, and (3) a KCC that coordinates eviction across shards via short-lived leases to prevent simultaneous mass-eviction (which caused transient OOMs on some dedicated machines).
migration_plan: Merge feature branch behind feature flag 'adaptive-batcher-kcc',
Run unit + integration tests in CI; load test against perf harness (gen-std-100k) to validate throughput and tail latency,
Deploy to internal staging with KCC running in observer-only mode for 48h, collecting metrics,
Canary deploy to 1% of hosted API traffic for 24h with automatic rollback triggers on p99 regressions or cache hit drop >5%,
Incremental ramp to Dedicated pools: start with non-critical tenant pool then expand once stable,
Full-on rollout after 7 days of stable canaries and sign-off from SRE and Platform.
risks: Regression in p50/p90 due to lane-sizing miscalibration (mitigated by per-tenant tuning and feature toggles),
KCC lease churn could introduce small additional RPCs; will be batched and rate-limited,
Dependency upgrade to libkvc v2.3 surfaces a subtle memory reclamation bug on older CUDA runtimes — mitigation: pin CUDA compatibility matrix and run targeted smoke tests.
implementation_notes: Technical approach: replace global batcher mutex with per-lane atomic counters and ring buffers; implement hysteresis window with configurable high/low thresholds to grow/shrink lanes only after dwell time; move eviction callbacks out of request-completion path to a background eviction worker that consults KCC for safe reclaim windows. KCC exposes a small protobuf API (AcquireLease/ReleaseLease/QueryOwner) and keeps metadata in in-memory sharded maps with periodic checkpointing to disk for crash recovery. Telemetry: emit lane_count, lane_occupancy, hysteresis_events, kcc_leases_issued, kcc_evictions_triggered. Also add flamegraph targets for hot-path tracing.
